external_deps: Ollama, llama.cpp, MLX, Docker Model Runner or LM Studio (optional, for downloads and benchmarks)

review.tagline: Rust tool that checks which LLMs fit your RAM, CPU and GPU
review.summary: llmfit detects CPU cores, RAM, GPU and VRAM (NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, Intel OneAPI, Apple Silicon), then scores a model catalog on fit, speed, quality and context across quantizations such as GGUF, AWQ, GPTQ and EXL2. It runs as a TUI, a CLI with JSON output, or an HTTP API and web dashboard via `llmfit serve`. Speed figures are estimates from a memory-bandwidth model, and `llmfit bench` can measure real tok/s against a running provider.
review.audience: Self-hosters choosing which local LLMs and quantizations their hardware can run
strengths: Detects NVIDIA, AMD, Intel and Apple Silicon hardware, including multi-GPU and unified memory
Handles MoE models, so memory estimates reflect active parameters rather than total size
JSON CLI output and REST endpoints (/api/v1/system, /api/v1/models) suit scripts and pipelines
Installs via Scoop, Homebrew, MacPorts, uv/pip, cargo or a multi-arch Docker image
weaknesses: Speed and fit numbers are estimates unless measured on your hardware or matched to community results
Does not serve models itself; it recommends and benchmarks against Ollama, llama.cpp, MLX and similar
Windows binaries may ship unsigned if the signing job fails
Model catalog is built in, so new models need a release or a custom-model entry
needs: Needs Ollama, llama.cpp, MLX, Docker Model Runner or LM Studio (optional, for downloads and benchmarks)
